source_refs.note: 6. Venturi Relation: a main subheading of 5.12 Uses of Bernoulli's principle, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 109-109.

blocks.text: Consider a pipe within which a fluid of density ρ is flowing through different areas of cross-section as shown in the Fig. 5.22.
Let A₁ be the cross-sectional area at wide end and A₂ be the cross-sectional area at narrow portion.
Suppose that v₁ and v₂ be the flow speeds at the wide and narrow portions respectively. Pressure P₁ and P₂ indicate the liquid pressure at both the portions by connecting the limbs of the manometer.

blocks.alt: A horizontal pipe with a wide part A1 on the left, a narrow throat A2 in the middle and a wide part again on the right. Three streamlines squeeze together through the throat; v1 is marked in the wide part and v2 in the throat. A U-tube manometer below joins the wide part and the throat: the level under the wide part, P1, is lower, and the level under the throat, P2, is higher by h.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.22: Venturi meter (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.22).
